en.title: Mega Man Legends 'New Media' Listing Hints at Franchise Return
en.summary: A cryptic listing for 'Mega Man Legends — New Media' on ACTRA Toronto's 'What's Shooting' page has ignited fan speculation about a potential comeback for the beloved PlayStation series. While the listing was quickly removed, screenshots have fueled hopes for a new game, movie, or TV show.
en.body:
The digital ether is abuzz once again with rumors of the **Mega Man Legends** franchise's return. A now-deleted listing on ACTRA Toronto's 'What's Shooting' page, a public database for projects registered with Canada's performers' union, hinted at a 'Mega Man Legends — New Media' project. Spotted by eagle-eyed fans and publications before its swift removal, the listing included a tentative start date of September 14, 2026, and an end date of December 1, 2026, with casting described as 'in-house.' This vague 'New Media' designation has sent fans into a frenzy, as it could signify anything from a new video game to a television series or even a film.

Capcom has shown a renewed interest in bringing its classic IPs to the screen. Following the success of the **Resident Evil** film adaptation and the upcoming **Street Fighter** movie, the company has been exploring live-action potential for **Mega Man** itself. A **Mega Man** movie was confirmed back in 2018, with directors **Henry Joost** and **Ariel Schulman** attached, who expressed their excitement about the project in 2020. While details have been scarce, this new listing suggests that *something* is indeed in development, potentially signaling a significant expansion beyond just game compilations.

## A Resurgence for the Legends

The **Mega Man Legends** series, comprising **Mega Man Legends** and **Mega Man Legends 2**, holds a special place in the hearts of many gamers. Known for its unique cel-shaded graphics, open-world exploration, and a departure from the traditional platforming of the classic **Mega Man** titles, the series left fans yearning for more, particularly after the unresolved cliffhanger of its last installment. The absence of **Mega Man Legends** from Capcom's recent Legacy Collections, which have covered almost every other **Mega Man** sub-series, has only amplified the demand. The recent announcement during Udon Entertainment's San Diego Comic-Con 2026 panel confirms that a **Mega Man Legends** miniseries is officially in the works, reuniting writer **David Oxford** and artist **Mic Fong**, who previously collaborated on **Mega Man Legends Timelines #1**. This marks the first concrete step towards new **Mega Man Legends** content in years, though it is separate from the 'New Media' listing which could imply a larger project.

## The Fan Reaction and Future Possibilities

For years, the community has clamored for a return to the world of **Mega Man Legends**, with many hoping for a **Mega Man Legends 3** that never materialized. The ACTRA listing, however vague, reignited those hopes. While the confirmed Udon miniseries is exciting, the 'New Media' tag leaves the door wide open for other possibilities. Could this be the long-awaited game, or perhaps the **Mega Man** movie that has been in development hell for years? The timing also aligns with Capcom's ongoing strategy of leveraging its established franchises across multiple platforms. The prospect of a **Mega Man Legends** game, even a AA title developed by a smaller, passionate team, is something fans have openly discussed as a viable and welcome return.

## What's Next

While no official confirmation has been made regarding a new game or movie, the **Mega Man Legends** miniseries from Udon Entertainment is officially in development. Further details on the 'New Media' project, if it is indeed separate from the miniseries, have not yet been announced.

content_raw: A now-deleted listing for ‘Mega Man Legends — New Media’ was spotted on a ‘What’s Shooting’ page for ACTRA Toronto, hinting that a new game, film, or TV series in the franchise's 'Legends' series is in the works. Although it’s since been deleted, several publications were able to screenshot the listing before it was taken down. The project’s start date was listed as September 14, 2026, with an end date of December 1, 2026. Casting was listed as “in-house.” ACTRA Toronto’s What’s Shooting page is a public database that compiles ongoing projects that are registered with Canada’s performers’ union, the Alliance of Canadian Cinema, Television and Radio Artists. The Mega Man project’s ‘New Media’ label is especially intriguing, as this doesn’t necessarily denote that a new game is being made; rather, it’s vague enough to encompass any manner of projects, including movies or TV shows. A Mega Man Legends movie isn’t out of the question, especially given Capcom’s recent foray into the world of Hollywood films. Zach Cregger’s Resident Evil adaptation was wildly successful, and hopes are high for a sequel to Legendary’s Street Fighter flick. In fact, Capcom has been working toward a screen adaptation of Mega Man for some time; the developer confirmed that a movie was being made in 2018 , which was initially being handled by 20th Century Fox (now 20th Century Studios). Things were quiet for the next few years until 2020, when Henry Joost and Ariel Schulman, who were set to write and direct this movie, confirmed that it was still very much in production . “We are super excited about it. I think we’re going to have some big news about it soon. I can’t say all that much right now, but it’s a project very near and dear to our hearts and we’re psyched,” Joost said at the time. In 2021, Netflix announced that it was making a live action film based on Capcom’s legacy 2D platformer, which appeared to be unrelated to 20th Century’s Mega Man project. For now, it’s unclear if this newest listing is involved with either of those productions, and the slim information that's been provided is making fans' imaginations run wild. Of course, most players are keen for a Mega Man Legends remake, or at least another title in that particular series. The first Mega Man Legends game was released all the way back in 1998; a sequel came out in 2000, and a spin-off title, The Misadventures of Tron Bonne , launched in 1999. With Dual Override coming in 2027, and Capcom expressing an interest in reviving its older IP , it’s certainly possible that there’s already another Mega Man title in the works — and remakes of legacy games are proving to be a real hit right now, after all. For now, Mega Man fans can check out our interview with Dual Override’s Director Shinya Ikuta, Producer Hiroyuki Minamitani, Art Director Yuji Ishihara, and Art Director Shinsuke Komaki, where we asked them all about the game and what players can expect when it finally releases.
